mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate reduces the cost of capital for corporations, leading to higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 1.0% (as of t-1mo), with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being positive.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 6.5% in the past month, it signals weakening labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.5% (as of t-1mo), with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based slowdown in consumer demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline (as of t-2mo), with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high industrial production growth (above 2% annualized), the S&P 500 tends to underperform as the economy approaches capacity constraints, leading to negative returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 2% (annualized), with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) indicates a strengthening labor market that boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS growth is above 0.5% (monthly), with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being positive.

mechanism_narrative: When the year-over-year CPIAUCSL inflation rate exceeds 2.5%, it signals persistent inflation that may lead to tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when CPIAUCSL YoY exceeds 2.5%, with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) and monthly housing starts (HOUST) indicates a deepening economic slowdown, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline (as of t-4mo and t-2mo, respectively), with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being negative.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion regime, rising retail sales (RSAFS) signal strong consumer demand that supports corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when RSAFS growth is above 0.5% (monthly) during late-cycle expansion, with a t-test p-value > 0.05 for the mean return being positive.
